To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
phomactatrienes are biosynthesized from GGDP via the intermediates, phomactatrienol and phomactatrienic acid.

the cyclization product phomacta -1(14), 3, 7 - triene was isolated from Phomacta sp. and that the stereochemistry of its formation was determined by 13C NMR spectroscopic analysis of the cyclization product and by the results of incorporation of [1-13c]- and [1.2-13C 2] acetate.
the stereochemistry of GGDP cyclisation in the biosynthesis phomactins was determined to be syn, and that phomactins and taxanes share phomactatrienol as their common precursor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biosynthetic pathways of taxol and phomactins.
the stereochemical course of cyclization reactions leading to the formation of diterpene skeletons.
the elucidation of biosynthetic pathways of taxol and related taxane diterpenes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the biosynthesis of taxol proceeds via taxadien-5α-ol, taxadien-7β-ol, 5α-taxadiene-7β-yl acetate, 5α,7β-taxadiene-9α-ol acetate, and taxadiene-5α,9β-diol.
the stereochemical course of cyclization in the taxadiene and phomactatrienes is the same as in the gibberellic acid biosynthesis.
the biosynthetic pathway of phomactin A is as follows: acetate → mevalonate → farnesyl diphosphate → phomactatrienes → phomactaene → phomactin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
phomactin biosynthesis proceeds from the same intermediate, taxadiene, as that of taxol, but with a different cyclase.
phomactins and taxol are biosynthesized by a common pathway, but that phomactaene and baccatin are derived from different cyclization intermediates.
phomactins are synthesized from geranylgeranyl diphosphate (GGDP) via taxadiene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biosynthesis of the taxane and the phomactane skeletons is similar, with taxadiene as the common intermediate.
the stereochemical course of cyclization in the phomactins and taxol pathways is the same.
phomactins share a common intermediate, phomactatrienes, with taxadiene.
